newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off as TEM yields rise.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off as TEM yields rise.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off in slow trade as yields on benchmark six month Monetary Stabilization Notes, or TEMs, rose steeply in the Central Bank's Monday auction, traders said.

Trade was already flagging in a traditionally slow Easter holiday week, but "the rise in TEM yields also dampened the market," said Multinvest broker Reinaldo Uribe, who saw similar trade for the rest of the week.
Yields on six-month TEMs, which serve as the benchmark for wider interest rates, rose 257 basis points to 18.81 percent.
The bourse's 19-share .IBC index closed off 0.5 percent at 6,244.86 points, according to preliminary figures from the exchange, as among traded issues 13 fell, nine rose and 14 closed flat.
Merinvest's composite .MRCP index, which includes telephone company CANTV, slipped 0.64 percent to end at 96.73 points.
The day's trade volume was boosted to 28 million shares, worth 16 million bolivars ($34 million), on large cross trades in textile company Sudamtex A shares and Banco Mercantil B shares.
Sudamtex A ended flat, while Banco Mercantil B shares closed up 79.00 bolivars at 1399.00.
